project: ThreatSmith v0.4.0 — Threat Modeling as Agent Skills
description: Repackage the threat modeling frameworks as distributable Agent Skills (source of truth), add from-code/from-docs/pair modes, refactor the CLI to drive installed skills per stage (Model B), and ship a source-agnostic secure-coding consumption skill.

userStories.title: Canonical shared reference content as markdown
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want shared reference material stored canonically as markdown so skills can bundle it from a single source of truth.
acceptanceCriteria: STRIDE categories, OWASP Web/API/LLM/Mobile, and scanner-usage guidance each exist as canonical markdown files in one shared location.
Each reference file is self-contained and suitable for embedding into a skill's references/ directory.
The reference content reproduces the substance of the existing Python reference constants it replaces.
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Six canonical reference markdown files created in skills-src/_shared/references/ (stride-categories, owasp-web/api/llm/mobile-top-10, scanners)

userStories.title: 4QF+STRIDE skill sources with three modes
userStories.description: As a user, I want a threatsmith-stride-4q skill whose stages support from-code, from-docs, and pair modes so I can run the methodology directly in my coding agent.
acceptanceCriteria: A threatsmith-stride-4q skill exists with a SKILL.md and one stage file per stage under references/stages/ (5 files incl. report), writing the existing output filenames (01-system-model … 05-report).
SKILL.md prompts the user to choose a mode (from-code, from-docs, pair) when none is supplied and honors a supplied mode.
Each stage reads prior outputs by path from the output directory rather than expecting inlined text.
Each stage includes natural-language conditional guidance for when to consult the API/LLM/Mobile references.
from-docs framing instructs the agent to discover local docs and to fetch invoker-pointed external context (e.g., tickets/Confluence via MCP) without hardcoded paths.
Invoking the skill directly in from-code mode against a sample repo produces all five deliverables.
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Authored threatsmith-stride-4q skill source (SKILL.md + 5 stage files under references/stages/) with from-code/from-docs/pair mode handling, file-pointer prior-output reads, and conditional OWASP API/LLM/Mobile reference guidance.

userStories.title: PASTA skill sources with three modes
userStories.description: As a user, I want a threatsmith-pasta skill mirroring the stride-4q skill for the 7-stage PASTA methodology plus report.
acceptanceCriteria: A threatsmith-pasta skill exists with a SKILL.md and one stage file per stage under references/stages/ (8 files incl. report), writing the existing output filenames.
Mode handling (from-code/from-docs/pair), file-pointer prior-output access, and conditional reference guidance match the stride-4q skill.
from-docs framing instructs the agent to discover local docs and fetch invoker-pointed external context without hardcoded paths.
Invoking the skill directly in from-code mode produces all eight deliverables.
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Authored threatsmith-pasta skill source (SKILL.md + 8 stage files under references/stages/) mirroring stride-4q: from-code/from-docs/pair SDLC-phase modes, file-pointer prior-output reads, conditional OWASP API/LLM/Mobile guidance at stage 04, scanners via references/scanners.md at stage 05. Writes existing PASTA output filenames (01-objectives … 08-report).

userStories.title: Single-stage non-interactive skill entry point
userStories.description: As the CLI orchestrator, I need each framework skill to execute exactly one stage non-interactively given the stage, mode, output dir, and prior-output location.
acceptanceCriteria: Each framework skill can be invoked to run exactly one named stage non-interactively, given the stage, mode, output directory, and prior-output location.
A single-stage invocation writes only that stage's deliverable.
The single-stage output is consistent with the same stage produced during a full walkthrough.
Tests pass

userStories.title: Secure-coding consumption skill (plan / review)
userStories.description: As an engineer, I want a threatsmith-secure skill that injects an existing threat model into planning and code review, working regardless of how the threat model was produced.
acceptanceCriteria: A threatsmith-secure skill exists supporting plan and review modes, prompting for a mode when none is supplied.
plan mode emits a security augmentation layer (requirements/constraints/checklist) and does not overwrite or own the planning document, so it composes with external planning skills.
review mode reports threats and mitigations relevant to a provided diff/change set, flagging uncatalogued threats and missing required mitigations.
The skill reads a threat-model directory of markdown and requires neither ThreatSmith-specific filenames nor metadata.json.
The skill works against a hand-authored threat-model directory.
Tests pass

userStories.title: Skill build, reference sync, and committed artifacts
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want a build step that syncs each skill's references and writes self-contained skills to a committed, CI-verified location.
acceptanceCriteria: A build step assembles each skill in self-contained form by syncing its required shared references into its references/ directory.
The build writes self-contained skills to a committed build location, and each built skill contains only the references it uses.
A committed built skill can be copied directly into an agent's skills directory and used without running a build.
Editing a canonical reference and rebuilding updates every skill that uses it.
CI runs the build and fails when the committed built skills differ from a fresh build.
Tests pass

userStories.title: Orchestrator + assembler refactor to Model B with file-pointer context
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the orchestrator to drive the installed skill per stage and pass prior context by file pointer so per-stage isolation is preserved with leaner context.
acceptanceCriteria: For each stage, the orchestrator invokes the engine to run the named installed skill for that single stage in the selected mode.
The assembler composes a per-stage instruction (skill name, stage, mode, output directory, prior-output location) instead of assembling prompt text.
Prior-stage context is passed by file pointer; no prior-stage text is inlined into prompts.
The CLI no longer performs scanner detection (detect_scanners removed); scanner usage is delegated to the agent via the shared reference file.
Output validation against the framework's expected output filenames is preserved.
Tests pass

userStories.title: Framework packs reduced to orchestration metadata
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want the Python framework packs stripped of prompt strings and reduced to stage metadata pointing at the providing skill.
acceptanceCriteria: Framework packs no longer contain STAGE_PROMPT constants or build_prompt functions.
Each pack retains stage order, expected output filenames, the report stage, and an identifier for its providing skill.
No prompt text remains in Python modules.
The framework registry, get_framework, and list_frameworks continue to work.
Tests pass

userStories.title: Retire conditional-injection logic
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want the keyword-matching conditional reference logic removed so reference selection is handled by the agent via in-prompt guidance.
acceptanceCriteria: The keyword-matching conditional-injection utility (conditions.py and its api_detected/llm_detected logic) is removed.
No code path performs keyword matching to inject references.
Tests that referenced the removed logic are updated or removed.
Tests pass

userStories.title: Built skills bundled as package data
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want the built skills shipped inside the package so the CLI distribution is self-contained and install-skills has a source to copy from.
acceptanceCriteria: The built (self-contained) skill directories are included as package data in the built distribution.
The packaging process uses the committed/freshly-built skills so bundled skills are current.
Tests pass

userStories.title: threatsmith install-skills command
userStories.description: As a user, I want a command that installs the bundled skills into my agent's skills directory.
acceptanceCriteria: threatsmith install-skills copies the bundled built skills into the engine's skills directory.
Re-running refreshes/overwrites an existing install.
The command reports what was installed and where.
The install target accounts for the selected engine.
Tests pass

userStories.title: Pre-run skill validation (validate-or-exit)
userStories.description: As a user, I want the CLI to tell me to install skills if they're missing rather than failing obscurely mid-run.
acceptanceCriteria: Before a run, the CLI verifies the skill required by the selected framework is installed.
If missing, the CLI exits with a clear message instructing the user to run threatsmith install-skills.
If present, the run proceeds normally.
Tests pass

userStories.title: CLI --mode flag and metadata mode field
userStories.description: As a user, I want to select from-code or from-docs on the CLI and have the mode recorded in metadata.
acceptanceCriteria: --mode accepts from-code (default) and from-docs; pair is rejected with a message that pair is skill-only.
The selected mode is passed to each per-stage skill invocation.
metadata.json records the mode, and scanner-availability fields are no longer written.
Tests cover default mode, explicit from-docs, and rejection of pair.
Tests pass

userStories.title: E2E — CLI drives stride-4q skill end to end
userStories.description: As a developer, I want an end-to-end test that the CLI orchestrates the stride-4q skill through all stages via Model B with file-pointer context.
acceptanceCriteria: With a mock engine, a full --framework stride-4q run produces all five deliverables.
Each stage invocation targets the named skill and a single stage in the selected mode.
metadata.json records framework stride-4q and the mode.
The orchestrator does not inline prior-stage text.
Tests pass

userStories.title: E2E — PASTA regression via skills
userStories.description: As a developer, I want an end-to-end test confirming PASTA still produces its eight deliverables under the skill-driven architecture.
acceptanceCriteria: With a mock engine, a full --framework pasta run produces all eight deliverables with the original filenames.
metadata.json records framework pasta and the mode.
Tests pass

userStories.title: E2E — consumption skill against a sample threat model
userStories.description: As a developer, I want an end-to-end test that the consumption skill operates on a sample threat-model directory without ThreatSmith-specific metadata.
acceptanceCriteria: plan mode produces a security augmentation output referencing a sample model's threats/mitigations.
review mode flags a planted unmitigated-threat gap in a sample diff.
Both modes run with no metadata.json present.
Tests pass

userStories.title: Documentation update
userStories.description: As a user, I want the README and docs updated to explain skills, modes, installation, and the consumption workflow.
acceptanceCriteria: README documents install-skills, --mode, the three generation modes, and direct vs CLI usage.
README documents the secure-coding consumption skill (plan/review) and its composability with planning workflows.
README documents the first-run requirement to install skills as a change from prior versions.
Tests pass
